tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: PowerShell 7+ (pwsh)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` ARE available and work like bash. Prefer `cmd1 && cmd2` over `cmd1; cmd2` when cmd2 should only run if cmd1 succeeds.
   - Ternary (`$cond ? $a : $b`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are available.
   - Default file encoding is UTF-8 without BOM.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. # Meshy AI — Workflow Guide

Every create tool returns {task_id, status}, except meshy_creative_lab, which waits and returns the finished model. Wait for it with meshy_get_task_status (task_type is inferred when omitted), then meshy_download_model.
Earlier results: meshy_list_models lists finished 3D models (image-to-3d by default; task_types widens it); meshy_list_tasks lists tasks of any status (default: text-to-3d, image-to-3d, multi-image-to-3d, text-to-image, image-to-image; task_types widens it, so an empty default list does not mean there are no printing, rigging or Creative Lab tasks).

## Rule 1: Cost Confirmation
Before calling ANY tool that costs credits, ask which ai_model to use where there is a choice (prefer an explicit one), present the cost and wait for user confirmation.

| Tool | Credits |
|------|---------|
| meshy_text_to_3d (preview, mesh only) | 20 (meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6), 5 (meshy-6-lite, meshy-t2, meshy-t2.5) |
| meshy_image_to_3d / meshy_multi_image_to_3d | table below |
| meshy_text_to_3d_refine / meshy_retexture | 10 (15 with texture_resolution "8k") |
| meshy_remesh / meshy_rig (incl. walking + running) / meshy_uv_unwrap | 5 |
| meshy_animate | 3 per action |
| meshy_text_to_motion | 10 (prime) / 3 (swift) |
| meshy_repair_printability / meshy_process_multicolor / meshy_auto_split | 10 |
| meshy_convert / meshy_resize | 1 |
| meshy_creative_lab | 36; keycap 62; fidget-collapsible 6 |
| meshy_text_to_image / meshy_image_to_image | nano-banana 3, nano-banana-2 6, nano-banana-2-lite 3, nano-banana-2-1 4, nano-banana-pro 9; GPT Image models (gpt-image-2, gpt-image-2-5-flare, gpt-image-2-5-sunburst) 9 text / 12 image |
| analyze printability, balance, usage, animation library, status, list, download | free |

| image / multi-image ai_model | mesh only | + 2K/4K texture | + 8K texture |
|---|---|---|---|
| meshy-7.1 / latest / meshy-6 (and deprecated meshy-7) | 20 | 30 | 35 |
| meshy-6-lite | 5 | 15 | — (2K only) |
| meshy-t2 / meshy-t2.5 (single-image Smart Topology) | 5 | 15 | 20 |

Ultra geometry (geometry_resolution "2k"/"4k") adds 5 on meshy-7.1 / latest. Confirm the 8K and Ultra surcharges explicitly.
Prices match https://docs.meshy.ai/en/api/pricing as of 2026-10-12; point the user there if a number looks off.

## Rule 2: Never Re-create a Task You Are Unsure About
If a create call fails with a timeout, network error or 5xx, the task may still have been created and charged. Check meshy_list_tasks (task_type = that task's type) for it before calling the create tool again. A wait that times out leaves the task running: poll the same task_id again.

## Rule 3: Determine Output Format BEFORE Generating
target_formats is fixed at creation time (3mf only when listed), so ask about the intended use first.

## Rule 4: Identify the Use Case, Then Confirm with User
Determine which scenario below best matches, present a suggested plan to the user, and confirm before executing. When a request spans several scenarios (e.g. A then L), combine their steps and confirm the combined plan.

---

## Scenario A: 3D Printing (white model)
Trigger: user mentions print, slicer, figurine, miniature, statue, physical model — single-color.
Suggested flow:
1. Detect installed slicers (meshy_send_to_slicer, slicer_type:"auto") — present list, save for later
2. Generate an untextured model with target_formats:["obj"]: meshy_text_to_3d (preview), or meshy_image_to_3d with should_texture:false
3. Wait for completion
4. Optionally check printability (meshy_analyze_printability, free). If it reports errors, either repair with model_url = the generation task's OBJ URL (model_urls.obj) so the result stays OBJ — on that route pass printer_type and intended_print_longest_side_mm, since intended_print_height_mm only works with task / GLB input — or repair by the analyze task, then meshy_convert the repaired GLB to obj (1 credit). print_ready only fixes OBJ
5. Download the OBJ (the repair task's, if repaired) with print_ready=true and print_height_mm (local Z-up fix and scaling)

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. When the request says who else will read or use the work, such as a team, a manager or a reviewer, or where it will be posted or presented, such as a channel or a meeting, Claude publishes it. # Re-review rulings — 2026-10-27 (delegated: the user said "just use best judgment")

Marker for every edit that applies one of these: *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling Rn)*.
In-text record where a decision is stated: "Resolved 2026-10-27 — delegated ruling Rn (re-review; user delegated to best judgment): ..."
These rulings never reverse a prior user ruling; they settle consequences the user's rulings left ambiguous or unimplementable.

## General rules (G)
- G1 Owner wins: where two GDDs disagree on a value, field, unit or contract, the registry `source:` GDD wins and the other conforms. If the thing is unregistered, the PUBLISHER of the field/signal/value wins and the consumer conforms.
- G2 Specialist disagreements: follow the creative-director's stated resolution in that GDD's disagreements list. Where the CD said "the user should choose", take the CD's stated lean.
- G3 Carried-over blockers (flagged "still not fixed"/"carried over"): previous edits did not land. After each edit, Grep for the old wording and confirm it is gone everywhere in the GDD (body, examples, ACs, tuning tables, OQs).
- G4 ACs that contradict the GDD's own formulas: recompute from the formula at registry defaults; never weaken a formula to match an AC.
- G5 Division/overflow at boundaries: guard explicitly (e.g. avail == 0 -> share 0, everything unserved); state the guard in the formula and add a boundary AC.

## Cross-cutting rulings (R)
- R1 Restore epoch (consequence of X8/D16). Save/Load OWNS `restore_epoch` as a persisted integer in the save slot header (u32, starts 0). On every restore (death restart or load), Save/Load increments it and durably writes the header (atomic header-only write) BEFORE the first RUNNING tick, so reloading the same autosave twice, in-process or after a fresh process start, gives a new epoch each time. The kernel exposes it read-only in `kernel.clock` as (T, world_seed, restore_epoch) — sim-visible, pure. The KERNEL (command-simulation-layer.md) owns the one derivation for threat draws, counter
- R2 seq (kernel CR-4). The kernel stamps `seq` internally per (peer, source); callers never choose it; `submit()` stays void (fire-and-forget). A caller may attach an opaque `correlation` field (int) that the kernel echoes unchanged in the result/rejection event. Player Controller keys pre-play tokens by `correlation`. Update the kernel seq ACs (L883, L892, L902-904) and PC-7 together.
- R3 Completion sentinel (kernel CR-19b). Every owner callable receives `ctx`; results flow through ctx, never the return value: validate reports via ctx.ok() / ctx.reject(reason); snapshot via ctx.put(payload); apply(cmd, write_scope, ctx). Every callable's only return is `return ctx.complete()` (a typed token). No `-> void` owner callables.
- R4 Mouse aim. The Player Controller's form is canonical: cursor_aim_world = f_q + (cursor_vp - picture_centre) / k_eff, where f_q is the quantized camera position actually used for the frame. The Pipeline PUBLISHES f_q. Aim direction = cursor_aim_world - AIM_ORIGIN, with AIM_ORIGIN = floor(pos) + (0, AIM_ORIGIN_Y) (ruling D10); remove the chest-based subtraction from the Pipeline's D.14b/D.7. Cursor units: the fixer must VERIFY the unit of the cursor source (e.g. Viewport.get_mouse_position() under the Pipeline's canvas_items stretch wiring (ii)) against docs/engine-reference/godot/ and the 
- R5 Carry tell (consequence of X3). Owners: Attention owns the intake numbers and the ONE integrator (Attention's walk-in convention and tick accounting are canonical; Boarding quotes them); Boarding owns the live-choice acceptance (AC-BS-123) and its K definitions, stated with Attention's integrator; Derelict owns the route length (21-28 tiles, X3). Scope: the burden applies only to SALVAGE carry — an item carried that was picked up inside a non-home locus (derelict) — moving or standing, until dropped/installed/thrown; never to carrying at home or of the player's own kit. Pace-robustnes
- R6 Pod statuses (consequence of user ruling D60 "statuses run in the pod"). Suit's reading stands: the reserve drains, the cell drains while lit, source RESERVE. Web Map conforms: delete WM-17b's HOLD reading and close ASK-S2. Pillar-2 mitigation: the valve click plays only on the source TRANSITION edge (once when breath_src becomes RESERVE), never per run. Recompute every pod-leg figure from the registry's own leg formula at registry defaults (ARRIVE_SETTLE_TICKS default 45, not 180; the registry's formulas use 945 ticks per leg — verify in the registry before using) and state run counts 
- R7 PD1 static spill bound (user ruling D31: 'static authored spill <= 24 px'). The bound stays 24 px — it is the user's number. The home ship's spine_corridor (computed 26 px) must be brought within it by Derelict Authoring (light placement, fixture position or corridor dressing — the least invasive change; show the recomputed s <= 24). Lighting's AC-LO-69 stays per-push BLOCKING.
- R8 Units of a request field shared by producer and consumer (e.g. Perception LEVEL vs Audio): G1 — the producer defines the unit; the consumer converts. State the unit in both GDDs with the conversion.
- R9 Undesigned dependencies (VS/Alpha systems with no GDD): not a blocker; keep them listed as "undesigned — provisional contract" with the interface this GDD assumes.
- R10 Pending-confirmation defaults and PLACEHOLDER values are not changed by these rulings unless a blocker shows them internally inconsistent.
- R11 X14 (reference machine) stays OPEN: never name or invent a reference machine, build type or spec anywhere.
# 2D Lighting & Occlusion

> Authoring guidance: .claude/docs/templates/guidance/game-design-document-guide.md (load per-section as you author — do not read entirely).

> **Status**: Designed
> **Author**: user + technical-artist, godot-shader-specialist, engine-programmer, creative-director (via /design-system, autonomous; orchestrated run 2026-10-26)
> **Last Updated**: 2026-10-27 (first formal design review; user rulings applied the same day)
> **Last Verified**: 2026-10-26 (statuses of dependent systems re-verified 2026-10-27)
> **Implements Pillar**: P1 The World Never Lies (primary — the drawn edge of every real light is the edge the simulation queries: hard cones end at `reach_px` ±1 px, soft pools end at `r_off` ±1 px (the latch-release radius, with the approach prompt `band_px` inside it, LO-7), occlusion is true occlusion with no vignette, fog or mask, and lamp brightness rides the Graph's closed consequence channel so no hallucination can change it); P3 The Web Watches (primary — emission is exposure: every running loop is a lantern drawn here, going dark is legible as light, and Attention's light-side tell is rendered as a gutter in the world, never as a meter). **Serves**: P4 Sanity Rewrites Reality (channel owner, not content owner: Lighting owns the one place a light-shaped lie may be drawn, a leaking overlay on a Lighting-owned layer, and guarantees the real light beneath it never moves); P2 Dread Before Chaos (the beacon sweep, the gutter and fault glows appearing on the Graph tick are the light channel of the 10–30 s tell, all inside the flash governor); P5 Deeper Is Richer, Loss Is Not Total (weakly: depth sets only the ambient-floor ordering, never reach or hue, so the ring ordering is not a difficulty dial)
> **Creative Director Review (CD-GDD-ALIGN)**: CONCERNS → REVISED 2026-10-26 (4 items applied)
> **Design Review (first formal /design-review, 2026-10-27)**: REVISED. 5 BLOCKING findings and the clear RECOMMENDED findings applied; every edited paragraph or row carries *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. The creative contract this revision protects: **the drawn edge equals the prompt edge** (LO-7), at every tier, rung and pass. Items that needed a person's call were ruled by the user on 2026-10-27 (next line).
> **User rulings (design-review decisions, 2026-10-27)**: the user ruled "I agree with all of your recommendations on those decisions" and answered "yes to all" on the held list. Applied here as **user rulings**: D31 (the PD-1/PD-1b residual bounds are accepted as scoped MVP exceptions, Open Question 21), X2 (the docked pod's dock-room status glow is an ordinary lit fixture, LO-34), X9 (the flash counting unit ceil(N / 2) is ratified, LO-22), D24 (`BEAM_SPILL` shape row 11, LO-35), and the confirmations D20-D23 (Emitter State's four provisional rulings stand; darkness is never a sanity cost). Applied as **defaults confirmed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R20)**: D32 (Emitter State adopts `SWITCH_MIN_SPACING_TICKS`; no Lighting exception), D33 (Open Questions 1-5 and 23 take their current defaults), D79/X10 (`reduce_flashing` defaults ON at first launch). **X14 closed 2026-10-28 (delegated ruling R12):** the reference machines are RM-DESKTOP and RM-DECK and the build is a Godot 4.7.2 release export (`project.yaml` `qa.min_spec`); Lighting's performance figures are pending spike measurement on them (Open Question 28). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R12)* The 2026-10-26 CD-GDD-ALIGN approval predates these amendments. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*
> **Re-review (2026-10-27)**: REVISED. The four BLOCKING findings are resolved (stand-in clamp withdrawn; the pool radius read from Emitter State's `r_lit_px` chain with the `r_off_px` publication agreed 2026-10-28; the darkening contract for characters, web, filaments and horrors under carrier B; the 24 px bound kept per delegated ruling R7, with `spine_corridor` owed by Derelict Authoring) and the clear RECOMMENDED findings applied; every edited paragraph or row carries *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*. Open Questions 31-36 are new. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*
> **Cross-GDD fix pass (2026-10-28)**: `r_off_px` is now read from Emitter State's 17-field view (Lighting no longer runs the chain; Open Question 25 resolved), the `BEAM_SPILL` foot pool is read through `beam_spill(beam_id)` (LO-5, LO-35), AC-LO-28 now tests the hash-gap onsets of D.15, X14 is closed by R12 (RM-DESKTOP, RM-DECK; Open Question 28 keeps only the GPU sub-budget). *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*

content.content:
**LO-15. Light textures: formats, generation and the layout choice (registry: `light_texture_layout`).** Per ART 8.3: `light_` textures are greyscale 8-bit PNG with soft alpha allowed and linear filter; 2048 for the beam shapes and the beacon, 512 for pools (deployable, glowstick, lantern and fault glow share one), 1024 for the fixture; the importer `size_limit` is 1024 under pass A and 2048 under pass B, with mipmaps off under A and on under B (ART 8.4 preset). Hard-edged textures carry an authored edge band of `EDGE_TEXELS` texels (placeholder 2, range 1-2: 3 and 4 fail the ±1 px contract by construction, D.9) so the edge is one base px under pass A and 1-2 screen px under pass B (the pass-A file uses `EDGE_TEXELS_A` 1, below). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)* Hard-edged beam and beacon textures import **lossless** (block compression moves the edge by sub-block amounts and would break the ±1 px lint); pool gradients may compress if the spike shows no banding. Every texture carries a **measured sidecar** (`edge_radius_texels`, `apex_offset_texels`) produced from the imported image, the runtime scale is `reach_px` or `r_draw` over the sidecar radius, and the reach lint becomes a headless image test: `|reach_px − edge_radius_texels × texture_scale| ≤ 0.1` base px at every `reach_px` the shape can take (the lint's own tolerance, kept separate from the measured ±1 px budget of D.9 so the two do not double-count, AC-LO-6); a sidecar that disagrees with its image fails the build. **Texture layout is per shape and is decided by a lateral fit test, not left as a spike coin-flip** (design review: the square cannot hold the fan). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The **lateral fit test**: a layout is valid iff, for every HARD row, `reach_px × sin(θ_max) + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX ≤ quad half-width`, where `θ_max` is the largest angle from the aim axis that the sector reaches (the half-angle for rows 1, 2, 4 and 8; 206 + 114 units = 28.1° for row 3) and `D_tex` is texels per base px; it is a lint over the five HARD rows and is measured on the rendered image by AC-LO-72. The art bible's 2048² square with the apex at the midpoint of one edge has a quad half-width of `reach_px / 2` and passes for the narrow cone (80.1 + 0.4 + 8 against 192), the beacon (131.6 + 0.4 + 8 against 192) and the split (158.3 + 0.3 + 8 = 166.6 against 168, margin 1.4 px). It **fails for the fan**: the registry half-angle 683 units is 60.0°, so the sector needs 168 × sin 60° = 145.5 px of half-width plus band and margin against the 84 px the square gives, and the flanks are clipped by about 70 px, over 40 % of the fan's lateral reach (a cone the simulation lights and the screen draws dark, a P1 lie). It also **fails for the wide beam**: 143.9 + 0.2 + 8 against 144, zero margin, so the edge band is clipped at the corners. The default layout is therefore **narrow, beacon, split: the art bible square; wide and fan: the tight non-square box**, with the apex at the midpoint of the back edge (the edge across the aim axis), axial extent `A = reach_px + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex`, lateral extent `B = 2 × (reach_px × sin θ_max + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX)`, and the longer of the two set to the importer limit (2048 under pass B, 1024 under pass A, ART 8.4 preset), which fixes `D_tex`. The tight box is also offered for narrow, beacon and split as a memory option. It requires non-square textures `[BIN]` and changes the ART 8.3/8.4 wording (Cross-References C row 18). Figures below are arithmetic on `LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX` 8 and `EDGE_TEXELS` 2 (ESTIMATE until step 2):

| Shape (row) | Layout | `A × B` (base px) | Texels, pass B | `D_tex` pass B / A | `a_tex` (base px) | Memory pass B, no mips (1 byte per texel) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wide (1) | tight box | 296.3 × 304.3 | 1994 × 2048 | 6.73 / 3.36 | (−148, 0) | 3.89 MiB |
| narrow (2) | square | 384 × 384 | 2048 × 2048 | 5.33 / 2.67 | (−192, 0) | 4.00 MiB (tight option 2048 × 924: 1.80 MiB) |
| split (3) | square | 336 × 336 | 2048 × 2048 | 6.10 / 3.05 | (−168, 0) | 4.00 MiB (tight option 2048 × 1982: 3.87 MiB) |
| fan (4) | tight box | 176.3 × 307.6 | 1174 × 2048 | 6.66 / 3.32 | (−88, 0) | 2.29 MiB |
| beacon (8) | square | 384 × 384 | 2048 × 2048 | 5.33 / 2.67 | (−192, 0) | 4.00 MiB (tight option 2048 × 1462: 2.86 MiB) |

**Memory, recomputed (ESTIMATE, 1 byte per texel; AC-LO-54).** Pass B: the five beam and beacon textures are 18.18 MiB, the fixture (1024²) 1.00 MiB and the shared pool (512²) 0.25 MiB, 19.43 MiB without mipmaps; with mipmaps on the beams (required for the minified shapes, LO-16) the beams are 24.2 MiB and the set 25.9 MiB; with the tight box for all five shapes the beams are 14.7 MiB (19.6 MiB with mipmaps) and the set 21.3 MiB. Pass A (importer limit 1024, mipmaps off): 4.54 MiB of beams plus 1.25 MiB of pools, 5.79 MiB. `FAMILY17` adds 4.25 MiB. The world viewport's `hdr_2d` colour target (RGBA16F, 8 bytes per pixel: 1.8 MiB at the 640×360 field under pass A, 15.8 MiB at 1080p and 63.3 MiB at 2160p under pass B, ESTIMATE `[UNV]`), the glow buffers and the shadow atlas are additional and are not in the art bible's light-texture line. Pass B with mipmaps exceeds the ART 8.6 20 MB light-texture line (25.9 MiB, or 21.3 MiB with every beam tight): a CONFLICT for the art-director and the technical-director (Open Question 27), with mitigations in order: the tight box for all five shapes, mipmaps only on the shapes minified more than 4x, pass A as the default. **Under the default layout the apex is at a texture edge, so `apex_offset_texels` in the sidecar is non-zero and `a_tex` in `beam_offset` (LO-10) is non-zero under both shadow-origin outcomes** (for the wide beam at pass B, `a_tex` = (−148, 0) base px). Whether the importer expands greyscale to RGBA8 (memory x4), whether textures are sampled from an engine atlas (no mipmaps), and which channel carries the profile (a squared profile would shorten the apparent reach) are `[UNV]` with probes at step 2 (2a, 2b). Textures are loaded once at boot behind the hold quad; nothing is loaded in play. **Re-review *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (spike step 2 inputs, decided here so step 2 measures one thing):** (1) *Two files per hard shape.* One `.import` carries one `size_limit`, so pass A and pass B cannot share a file: each hard shape ships `light_<shape>_a.png` (importer limit 1024, mipmaps off, band `EDGE_TEXELS_A` 1) and `light_<shape>_b.png` (limit 2048, mipmaps on, band `EDGE_TEXELS` 2), each with its own `.import` and measured sidecar; the pools share one 512 file for both passes. If both passes can be selected in play the two sets are resident together (pass A adds 5.79 MiB to the pass B figures above; Open Question 27 carries the sum) `[UNV]`. (2) *Pass A texture decided:* the pass-A file is authored with a 1-texel band, because a 2-texel band left the pass-A edge budget 0.025 base px of margin (D.9). (3) *Axial fit test, beside the lateral one:* a layout is valid only if `reach_px + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX ≤ A_quad`, where `A_quad` is the quad's extent along the aim axis from the apex. The tight boxes meet it by construction (`A` is defined as that sum). **The art bible's squares do not:** with the apex at the midpoint of one edge `A_quad` = the side = `reach_px`, so the narrow cone and the beacon need 384 + 0.4 + 8 = 392.4 against 384, and the split 336 + 0.3 + 8 = 344.3 against 336, and the outer half of the edge band and the whole safety margin are clipped by the quad's far edge. Step 2 resolves it either by growing the side to `A` (that lowers `D_tex` by about 2 %: narrow and beacon 5.33 to 5.22, split 6.10 to 5.95, which moves no D.9 edge budget by more than 0.01 base px and no screen-pixel width by more than 0.07; every `D_tex`-derived figure in D.9 to D.12 is quoted at the nominal value and stays an ESTIMATE until step 2) or by the tight box for those shapes (the memory option above). (4) *Probes added to step 2:* the filter each light texture is sampled with, NEAREST against LINEAR, because the project pins NEAREST as the default filter and a per-light control is unknown (2c), and the capacity and resident VRAM of the engine's light atlas against five 2048 textures (2d).

**LO-16. Zoom changes no light value; what a rung does change (the per-rung thread).** The ladder is implemented through the world viewport's logical size (PIPE C6, D.5), never `Camera2D.zoom`. Every light member that is a length (`texture_scale`, `offset`, `range_*`, `position`) is in **base px**, hence **independent of `k_z` under both passes**; Lighting has no zoom handler. A rung changes only: (i) how many base px a screen pixel covers (the hard edge is `k_z` screen px wide under pass A and 1-2 screen px under pass B; `edge_width_screen_px`); (ii) the lit-pixel count (`per_rung_lit_pixels`): pass A shades `floor(W / k_z) × floor(H / k_z)`, pass B the window area at every rung, so **pass A at `k_z` 1 costs the same lit pixels as pass B at any rung** (1080p: 2,073,600, which is 9x the default 640x360 field of 230,400; 1440p: 3,686,400, 16x; the Deck at 1280x800 `expand`: 1,024,000, 4x its own 640x400 default; 2160p: 8,294,400, 36x), so the "pass B is 9x pass A" lever disappears at the lowest rung and the LOD (LO-17) is needed under both passes; (iii) how many emitters and occluders are in view (answered by the LOD tier, demotion and the reach-set cap); (iv) under pass B how many screen px sample one texel (`texture_magnification`). With the per-shape layout of LO-15 the density `D_tex` is: narrow and beacon 5.33 and split 6.10 (the square, `2048 / reach_px`), wide 6.73 and fan 6.66 (the tight boxes, the long side 2048 over `max(A, B)`). Under pass B a texture is minified at every rung below that figure and magnified only above it: the narrow cone and the beacon above `k_z` 5.33 (the art bible's "~6x", ART 8.3 :1070-1075), which is reachable only at `k_z` 6 on 1440p (1.13x, the one 1440p case) and at `k_z` 6-8 on 2160p (1.13x, 1.31x, 1.50x), never on 1080p (ladder maximum 5) or the Deck (maximum 4); the split above 6.10 (2160p `k_z` 7-8, 1.15x and 1.31x); the wide beam above 6.73 (2160p `k_z` 7-8, 1.04x and 1.19x); the fan above 6.66 (2160p `k_z` 7-8, 1.05x and 1.20x). At `k_z` 1 on 1080p the wide beam is minified 6.7x under pass B, so mipmaps are required there. *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The rim softens slightly where a texture magnifies, accepted by ART 8.3, with the tight non-square layout of LO-15 as a remedy. **Shadow *positions* are `k_z`-independent** (occluders are in base px); shadow-edge stepping is a whole base px (= `k_z` screen px) under pass A and window resolution under pass B; the shadow edge error at maximum reach (about `2πR / N_ang` base px for an `N_ang`-sample shadow map: 1.18 px at 384 px reach for 2048 samples, ESTIMATE on an `[UNV]` model) is measured at spike step 3 for both passes. Off-screen lit objects stay lit and `state_hash` is identical at every rung (EM-30, AC-86): zoom changes nothing in the simulation. Both passes are specified in full (the pass A and pass B tables are in Formulas). content.content:
# Design Directory

When authoring or editing files in this directory, follow these standards.

## GDD Files (`design/gdd/`)

The 8 GDD sections, in order:
1. Overview — one-paragraph summary
2. Player Fantasy — intended feeling and experience
3. Detailed Rules — unambiguous mechanics
4. Formulas — all math defined with variables
5. Edge Cases — unusual situations handled
6. Dependencies — other systems listed
7. Tuning Knobs — configurable values identified
8. Acceptance Criteria — testable success conditions

**How many are REQUIRED depends on `modes.workflow`** — all 8 at `full`; 5 at
`standard` (Overview, Detailed Rules, Edge Cases, Dependencies, Acceptance
Criteria, plus Formulas when the system has math); none at `minimal`, where
`design/game-brief.md` is the design record instead of a GDD. Resolve the tier
before flagging a section as missing — see `.claude/docs/workflow-modes.md`.

> **Three other places already encode the tier rule** —
> `.claude/docs/coding-standards.md`, `.claude/rules/design-docs.md` and
> `.claude/hooks/validate-commit.sh`. This file is the copy a session working in
> `design/` reads first, so it must agree with them: demanding all 8 at
> `minimal` warns a jam project about six sections its own configuration says it
> does not need, which trains the user to ignore the warning.

**Section-name alias:** the GDD template and `/design-system` author section 3
as `## Detailed Design`; the standard calls it **Detailed Rules**. Same required
section — accept either heading, never rewrite one into the other.

**File naming:** `[system-slug].md` (e.g. `movement-system.md`, `combat-system.md`)

**Systems index:** `design/gdd/systems-index.md` — update when adding a new GDD.

**Design order:** Foundation → Core → Feature → Presentation → Polish

**Validation:** Run `/design-review [path]` after authoring any GDD.
Run `/review-all-gdds` after completing a set of related GDDs.

## Quick Specs (`design/quick-specs/`)

Lightweight specs for tuning changes, minor mechanics, or balance adjustments.
Use `/quick-design` to author.

## UX Specs (`design/ux/`)

- Per-screen specs: `design/ux/[screen-name].md`
- HUD design: `design/ux/hud.md`
- Interaction pattern library: `design/ux/interaction-patterns.md`
- Accessibility requirements: `design/accessibility-requirements.md`

Use `/ux-design` to author. Validate with `/ux-review` before passing to `/team-ui`.

> **Accessibility requirements sit OUTSIDE `design/ux/` on purpose.** They are a
> project-wide standard the per-screen specs consult, not a spec for one screen.
> `.claude/docs/workflow-catalog.yaml`, the Pre-Production, Production and Polish
> gates, and `/architecture-review` all check `design/accessibility-requirements.md`
> at that exact path. Do not "tidy" it under `design/ux/` — every one of those
> checks would stop matching, and the Technical Setup → Pre-Production gate would
> become unpassable. `/ux-design` states the same rule at its `accessibility` mode.

content.content:
**LO-15. Light textures: formats, generation and the layout choice (registry: `light_texture_layout`).** Per ART 8.3: `light_` textures are greyscale 8-bit PNG with soft alpha allowed and linear filter; 2048 for the beam shapes and the beacon, 512 for pools (deployable, glowstick, lantern and fault glow share one), 1024 for the fixture; the importer `size_limit` is 1024 under pass A and 2048 under pass B, with mipmaps off under A and on under B (ART 8.4 preset). Hard-edged textures carry an authored edge band of `EDGE_TEXELS` texels (placeholder 2, range 1-2: 3 and 4 fail the ±1 px contract by construction, D.9) so the edge is one base px under pass A and 1-2 screen px under pass B (the pass-A file uses `EDGE_TEXELS_A` 1, below). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)* Hard-edged beam and beacon textures import **lossless** (block compression moves the edge by sub-block amounts and would break the ±1 px lint); pool gradients may compress if the spike shows no banding. Every texture carries a **measured sidecar** (`edge_radius_texels`, `apex_offset_texels`) produced from the imported image, the runtime scale is `reach_px` or `r_draw` over the sidecar radius, and the reach lint becomes a headless image test: `|reach_px − edge_radius_texels × texture_scale| ≤ 0.1` base px at every `reach_px` the shape can take (the lint's own tolerance, kept separate from the measured ±1 px budget of D.9 so the two do not double-count, AC-LO-6); a sidecar that disagrees with its image fails the build. **Texture layout is per shape and is decided by a lateral fit test, not left as a spike coin-flip** (design review: the square cannot hold the fan). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* The **lateral fit test**: a layout is valid iff, for every HARD row, `reach_px × sin(θ_max) + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX ≤ quad half-width`, where `θ_max` is the largest angle from the aim axis that the sector reaches (the half-angle for rows 1, 2, 4 and 8; 206 + 114 units = 28.1° for row 3) and `D_tex` is texels per base px; it is a lint over the five HARD rows and is measured on the rendered image by AC-LO-72. The art bible's 2048² square with the apex at the midpoint of one edge has a quad half-width of `reach_px / 2` and passes for the narrow cone (80.1 + 0.4 + 8 against 192), the beacon (131.6 + 0.4 + 8 against 192) and the split (158.3 + 0.3 + 8 = 166.6 against 168, margin 1.4 px). It **fails for the fan**: the registry half-angle 683 units is 60.0°, so the sector needs 168 × sin 60° = 145.5 px of half-width plus band and margin against the 84 px the square gives, and the flanks are clipped by about 70 px, over 40 % of the fan's lateral reach (a cone the simulation lights and the screen draws dark, a P1 lie). It also **fails for the wide beam**: 143.9 + 0.2 + 8 against 144, zero margin, so the edge band is clipped at the corners. The default layout is therefore **narrow, beacon, split: the art bible square; wide and fan: the tight non-square box**, with the apex at the midpoint of the back edge (the edge across the aim axis), axial extent `A = reach_px + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex`, lateral extent `B = 2 × (reach_px × sin θ_max + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX)`, and the longer of the two set to the importer limit (2048 under pass B, 1024 under pass A, ART 8.4 preset), which fixes `D_tex`. The tight box is also offered for narrow, beacon and split as a memory option. It requires non-square textures `[BIN]` and changes the ART 8.3/8.4 wording (Cross-References C row 18). Figures below are arithmetic on `LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX` 8 and `EDGE_TEXELS` 2 (ESTIMATE until step 2):

| Shape (row) | Layout | `A × B` (base px) | Texels, pass B | `D_tex` pass B / A | `a_tex` (base px) | Memory pass B, no mips (1 byte per texel) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| wide (1) | tight box | 296.3 × 304.3 | 1994 × 2048 | 6.73 / 3.36 | (−148, 0) | 3.89 MiB |
| narrow (2) | square | 384 × 384 | 2048 × 2048 | 5.33 / 2.67 | (−192, 0) | 4.00 MiB (tight option 2048 × 924: 1.80 MiB) |
| split (3) | square | 336 × 336 | 2048 × 2048 | 6.10 / 3.05 | (−168, 0) | 4.00 MiB (tight option 2048 × 1982: 3.87 MiB) |
| fan (4) | tight box | 176.3 × 307.6 | 1174 × 2048 | 6.66 / 3.32 | (−88, 0) | 2.29 MiB |
| beacon (8) | square | 384 × 384 | 2048 × 2048 | 5.33 / 2.67 | (−192, 0) | 4.00 MiB (tight option 2048 × 1462: 2.86 MiB) |

**Memory, recomputed (ESTIMATE, 1 byte per texel; AC-LO-54).** Pass B: the five beam and beacon textures are 18.18 MiB, the fixture (1024²) 1.00 MiB and the shared pool (512²) 0.25 MiB, 19.43 MiB without mipmaps; with mipmaps on the beams (required for the minified shapes, LO-16) the beams are 24.2 MiB and the set 25.9 MiB; with the tight box for all five shapes the beams are 14.7 MiB (19.6 MiB with mipmaps) and the set 21.3 MiB. Pass A (importer limit 1024, mipmaps off): 4.54 MiB of beams plus 1.25 MiB of pools, 5.79 MiB. `FAMILY17` adds 4.25 MiB. The world viewport's `hdr_2d` colour target (RGBA16F, 8 bytes per pixel: 1.8 MiB at the 640×360 field under pass A, 15.8 MiB at 1080p and 63.3 MiB at 2160p under pass B, ESTIMATE `[UNV]`), the glow buffers and the shadow atlas are additional and are not in the art bible's light-texture line. Pass B with mipmaps exceeds the ART 8.6 20 MB light-texture line (25.9 MiB, or 21.3 MiB with every beam tight): a CONFLICT for the art-director and the technical-director (Open Question 27), with mitigations in order: the tight box for all five shapes, mipmaps only on the shapes minified more than 4x, pass A as the default. **Under the default layout the apex is at a texture edge, so `apex_offset_texels` in the sidecar is non-zero and `a_tex` in `beam_offset` (LO-10) is non-zero under both shadow-origin outcomes** (for the wide beam at pass B, `a_tex` = (−148, 0) base px). Whether the importer expands greyscale to RGBA8 (memory x4), whether textures are sampled from an engine atlas (no mipmaps), and which channel carries the profile (a squared profile would shorten the apparent reach) are `[UNV]` with probes at step 2 (2a, 2b). Textures are loaded once at boot behind the hold quad; nothing is loaded in play. **Re-review *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* (spike step 2 inputs, decided here so step 2 measures one thing):** (1) *Two files per hard shape.* One `.import` carries one `size_limit`, so pass A and pass B cannot share a file: each hard shape ships `light_<shape>_a.png` (importer limit 1024, mipmaps off, band `EDGE_TEXELS_A` 1) and `light_<shape>_b.png` (limit 2048, mipmaps on, band `EDGE_TEXELS` 2), each with its own `.import` and measured sidecar; the pools share one 512 file for both passes. If both passes can be selected in play the two sets are resident together (pass A adds 5.79 MiB to the pass B figures above; Open Question 27 carries the sum) `[UNV]`. (2) *Pass A texture decided:* the pass-A file is authored with a 1-texel band, because a 2-texel band left the pass-A edge budget 0.025 base px of margin (D.9). (3) *Axial fit test, beside the lateral one:* a layout is valid only if `reach_px + EDGE_TEXELS / D_tex + LIGHT_TEX_MARGIN_PX ≤ A_quad`, where `A_quad` is the quad's extent along the aim axis from the apex. The tight boxes meet it by construction (`A` is defined as that sum). **The art bible's squares do not:** with the apex at the midpoint of one edge `A_quad` = the side = `reach_px`, so the narrow cone and the beacon need 384 + 0.4 + 8 = 392.4 against 384, and the split 336 + 0.3 + 8 = 344.3 against 336, and the outer half of the edge band and the whole safety margin are clipped by the quad's far edge. Step 2 resolves it either by growing the side to `A` (that lowers `D_tex` by about 2 %: narrow and beacon 5.33 to 5.22, split 6.10 to 5.95, which moves no D.9 edge budget by more than 0.01 base px and no screen-pixel width by more than 0.07; every `D_tex`-derived figure in D.9 to D.12 is quoted at the nominal value and stays an ESTIMATE until step 2) or by the tight box for those shapes (the memory option above). (4) *Probes added to step 2:* the filter each light texture is sampled with, NEAREST against LINEAR, because the project pins NEAREST as the default filter and a per-light control is unknown (2c), and the capacity and resident VRAM of the engine's light atlas against five 2048 textures (2d).

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `reach_px` | int | 168 / 288 / 336 / 384 (rows 4 / 1 / 3 / 2 and 8) | `light_shape` REG:121 via the read view (`EM-8`) | the simulation's fade-out radius; for HARD rows it is also the drawn edge; never restated |

| `texture_scale` | float | 0.1486..0.375 | output | written to the light |

**Output Range:** pass B 0.1486 (wide) to 0.1875 (narrow, beacon); pass A 0.2978 (wide) to 0.375 (narrow, beacon). The sidecar is authoritative; the nominal figures are the layout's arithmetic. **Example:** narrow beam, `reach_px` 384: pass B 384 / 2048 = 0.1875, so the quad is 2048 × 0.1875 = 384 base px square with the apex at its left-middle; pass A (`size_limit` 1024) 384 / 1024 = 0.375. Both draw the edge at 384. Wide beam 288 (tight box): 1938 / 288 gives 0.1486 (B), 0.2978 (A); fan 168 (tight box): 0.1502 (B), 0.3009 (A). The cone's half-angle and rim level are baked into the texture from the shape table (LO-6), so narrow (12°) and beacon (20°) share a scale and differ in texture.

### D.9 Edge width in screen pixels

The `edge_width_screen_px` formula is defined as:

`w_A = k_z` (pass A); `w_B = max(1, EDGE_TEXELS × k_z / D_tex)` (pass B), `D_tex = edge_radius_texels / reach_px`; edge position error in base px: `err_A = 0.5 + 0.5 × EDGE_TEXELS_A / D_A` (the pass-A file's own band, *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*), `err_B = 0.5 × (EDGE_TEXELS + 1) / D_B`

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `k_z` | int | 1..`k_base` + 2 (`k_base` = the manual k below Auto if set, else `k_auto`; at `k_base` = `k_auto`: Deck 1-4, 1080p 1-5, 1440p 1-6, 2160p 1-8) | `PIPE D.5`, `zoom_out_k` | current rung *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass after design review)* |
| `EDGE_TEXELS` | int | 1..2; placeholder 2 (3 and 4 fail the contract by construction, see the example); the pass-B file | ★ ART 8.3 authored band, in imported texels | hard-edge band width, pass B |
| `EDGE_TEXELS_A` | int | 1 (decided; 2 leaves 0.025 base px) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | ★ ART 8.3 authored band of the separate pass-A file | hard-edge band width, pass A |
| `D_tex` | float | wide 6.73, split 6.10, narrow and beacon 5.33, fan 6.66 (pass B, LO-15's table); 3.36 / 3.05 / 2.67 / 3.32 (pass A) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | sidecar over `reach_px` | texels per base px |

**Output Range:** pass A: the edge is one base px, `k_z` screen px; pass B: 1.0 to 3.0 screen px across the ladder (table below). `err` plus the D.2 lint tolerance (0.1) must stay ≤ 1 base px, and the scale error must stay below that lint: `eps_scale` = |`texture_scale_used` − `reach_px / edge_radius_texels`| / (`reach_px / edge_radius_texels`), bounded by 0.1 / `reach_px` (0.00026 at reach 384). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* **Example:** narrow cone pass B at `k_z` 5: 2 × 5 / 5.33 = 1.88 screen px; at `k_z` 8 (2160p) 3.0, wider than ART 8.3's "1-2 screen px", accepted with the rim softening noted by ART 8.3 :1075. Error budget pass A narrow, with the pass-A file's 1-texel band (`EDGE_TEXELS_A` 1, LO-15): 0.5 + 0.5 × 1 / 2.67 = 0.687 base px, plus the D.2 lint's own 0.1 = 0.787 ≤ 1, so the ±1 px is not double-counted and about 0.21 is left for scale rounding and an import-filter shift (with the earlier 2-texel band it was 0.875 + 0.1 = 0.975 and only 0.025 was left) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*; pass B narrow 0.5 × 3 / 5.33 = 0.28; wide 0.22 (B) and 0.65 (A); fan 0.23 (B) and 0.65 (A). A band of 3 and 4 texels would give 1.0625 and 1.25 base px under pass A narrow (0.5 + 0.5 × n / 2.67; the earlier 1.125 and 1.375 were mis-computed) and fail by construction even before the lint's 0.1, hence the range 1-2 for pass B and 1 for pass A. The pass-A file is a separate, dedicated texture (LO-15) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; re-review)*

### D.10 Lit pixels per rung

The `per_rung_lit_pixels` formula is defined as:

`lit_px_A(k_z) = ⌊W / k_z⌋ × ⌊H / k_z⌋`; `lit_px_B = W × H`; `ρ = lit_px / (⌊W / k_auto⌋ × ⌊H / k_auto⌋)`; shadow step (ESTIMATE on an `[UNV]` model) `step_px = 2π × reach_px / SHADOW_ATLAS_PX`, in screen px `step_px × k_z` (pass B) or one base px = `k_z` screen px (pass A)

### D.11 Texture magnification

The `texture_magnification` formula is defined as:

`μ_B(k_z) = D_tex / k_z` texels per screen px (pass B), `μ_A = D_tex(A)` at every rung (pass A); a texture magnifies iff `μ < 1`, by `1 / μ`; the first magnifying rung is the smallest integer `k_z > D_tex`

**Variables:**

| Variable | Type | Range | Source | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `D_tex` | float | hard shapes: see D.9; soft pools: `edge_radius_texels / r_draw` | sidecar over the drawn radius | texels per base px of the drawn light |
| `k_z` | int | 1..8 | `PIPE D.5` | rung (pass B resolves lights at window resolution, so a base px is `k_z` screen px) |

**Output Range:** `μ` > 0; pass A is never magnified (hard shapes 2.67-6.10 texels per base px, mipmaps off, ART 8.4 preset); pass B is minified at every rung below `D_tex` and mipmaps are required there. First magnifying rung under pass B: **narrow and beacon `k_z` 6** (`D_tex` 5.33: 1440p `k_z` 6 at 1.13x; 2160p `k_z` 6 / 7 / 8 at 1.13x / 1.31x / 1.50x), **split `k_z` 7** (2160p: 1.15x, 1.31x), **wide `k_z` 7** (2160p: 1.04x, 1.19x), **fan `k_z` 7** (2160p: 1.05x, 1.20x); never on 1080p (maximum rung 5) or the Deck (maximum 4). *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* Soft pools: the fixture at `r_draw` 126 has `D_tex` 512 / 126 = 4.1 (B magnifies above `k_z` 4.1, harmless on a gradient); a glowstick at its last step has 256 / 21 = 12.2 texels per base px under pass A with mipmaps off, so `POOL_TEX_SWAP_PX` 48 swaps to a 128² pool texture below a drawn radius of 48 px if step 2 shows shimmer. **Example:** narrow cone, 1440p, `k_z` 6: 5.33 / 6 = 0.889, magnified 1.13x; 1080p, `k_z` 5: 5.33 / 5 = 1.07, minified; wide beam at `k_z` 1 on 1080p: 6.73 / 1 = 6.7x minified, so mipmaps are required.

content.content:
=== 32
**Index wording, reconciled.** The systems index (IDX:23, bullet 6, enumeration row 6, Recommended Design Order 9) says Lighting "owns the final Light2D values through a modifier contract: Attention flicker, horror light disturbance and Perception Filter decoys submit layered modifiers; the Filter may add decoy visuals but never changes the real reveal radius". This GDD keeps every clause and sharpens three words. "Final `Light2D` values" means every *value* member of every light (`enabled`, `energy`, `color`, `texture`, `texture_scale`, `offset`, shadow and range members); the local seat's beam *pose* members (`position`, `rotation`) are the Avatar Presenter's (Player Controller PC-5), so the two writers own disjoint member sets (LO-2). "Submit" means *publish state that Lighting reads* (KERN:117: "state that Lighting reads, not calls into Lighting"), never a call. "Attention flicker" is rendered as a **gutter** on fixtures (never the cryo-bay EMERGENCY lamp) and node lanterns only (the verb *flicker* is reserved for deployables, LO-30), an art-bible amendment this GDD requests rather than assumes. "Decoy visuals" are unlit overlays on a Lighting-owned layer and never lights (LO-21), which is what makes "never changes the real reveal radius" structural instead of a policy. The soft-cycle wording at IDX:266 ("Lighting never reads Attention") is superseded accordingly: Lighting reads Attention's published tell tier for the gutter recipe only and never derives reach, output, colour or edge from it.
=== 87
**Named rule 1: "A dip dims; a sag shrinks."** Power changes a lamp's *reach of readability*; nothing else does. Attention and Horror change only brightness, bounded at `MOD_FLOOR_PM`, and only on fixtures (not the cryo-bay lamp) and node lanterns. The two most important lamp events are therefore distinguishable by two cues, and the GDD is honest about which is reliable where (CD-GDD-ALIGN revision). The **readable radius** (`r_off`, the drawn edge, with `r_lit`, the prompt's approach edge, a few px inside it, LO-7) is unchanged by a dip and shrinks in a sag *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; that is the cue the HUD prompt, the Debug Overlay and AC-LO-30 measure. The **perceived** edge is a different thing: a 30 % dip lowers the pool's apex but not its radius, so on a dark Graphite floor the soft rim can look about 11 px closer for the 0.3-0.5 s of the dip (ESTIMATE, LO-7), and on those floors a still frame cannot be trusted to tell a dip from a sag by pool size. Pool size in a still frame is reliable on bright plates only. The redundant cue that holds everywhere, and that colour-blindness and a single captured frame cannot break, is the **temporal shape**: a dip is transient and returns to full, a sag is steady and stays (the same redundancy ART 2.4 demands for conserved versus lost). Open Question 19 (the playtest) is the arbiter of whether the temporal cue alone is enough.
=== 178
| FIXTURE (7) | `PointLight2D` | slot 6 rank 1 iff `subkind` EMERGENCY; else a lent slot 2-4 when wall-near and among the three nearest (LO-9); else none *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)* | `light_fixture` | 1 | warm-up; L1 gutter (EMERGENCY only); L2 and L3 (every subkind except EMERGENCY, LO-20) | FIXTURE (`#FFCC66`) | SOFT | `r_off` (126 px at 1000 permille for R 144; LO-7) |
=== 276
The chain is `m_mod = clamp(floor(M1 × M2 × M3 / 10^6), MOD_FLOOR_PM, 1000)` evaluated in integer permille and converted to the engine's float `energy` once, in the apply step (an order-independent integer inequality, and the same discipline the simulation uses), with the two transition envelopes (warm-up, cut-fade) multiplying afterwards. **Invariants, each with its own criterion:** (i) drawn energy never exceeds `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM × output_pm`, and the *steady modulation* (gutter, flicker, L2, L3 combined) never takes it below `MOD_FLOOR_PM` (placeholder 600 permille, range 400-800) of that value while `output_pm` > 0, so a dipping lamp never reads as a brownout tier; the floor does **not** apply to the warm-up and cut-fade envelopes, which are bounded start and stop ramps limited by their own duration and by the governor (orchestrator ruling: as originally worded, the floor contradicted both ramps); (ii) **exempt from L2 and L3: every BEAM (local and remote), the BEACON, every FAULT_GLOW and every DEPLOYABLE (glowsticks)**: beams are the human channel and "a truth anchor" (ART 2.7), beacon and fault glow are consequence-channel witnesses, and the glowstick is locked "steady, never flickers, then waning" by three documents; L2 and L3 apply to NODE_LANTERN and to FIXTURE except `subkind` EMERGENCY only (LO-20); (iii) **no layer touches `texture_scale`, `offset`, `range_*`, cone angle, `position`, `rotation` or `color` of a real light**, so the drawn edge stays at `reach_px` ±1 px (HARD) or `r_draw` ±1 px (SOFT) and the hue stays the token's hex at all times; this is what makes "never changes the real reveal radius" structural; (iv) on the same light, L3 outranks L2 (specific over general): while a disturbance is active it replaces the tell dip on that light, then both pass the governor; (v) "submission" is state Lighting reads from the submitter's published view and never a call. Rejected: additive offsets (they can exceed `output_pm`, breaking "a lamp never renders brighter than the power it is served"); last-writer-wins (non-deterministic with two sources).

L2 and L3: the Attention tell is a gutter, the Horror disturbance is a bounded dip (ruled R11; an art-bible amendment owed).** IDX:23 names "Attention flicker" as a modifier submitter and CON:233 names "creaking, flicker, filament movement" as Attention's world channels; an L2 with no submitter in any slice would be dead. The slot rule had nothing to add to the hash spread in its own example and left an overflow undefined. A floor-length tell (`TELL_MIN_TICKS` 600) never leaves tier 1, so one lamp can still show zero dips in it; Attention's other channels carry the tell there, Attention AT-9 / C2), carried by layer **M2** (`M2 = 1000 − DIP_DEPTH_PM` during a tell dip; the cryo lamp's baseline gutter is layer M1) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*, bounded by `MOD_FLOOR_PM` so it is never confused with starvation: a gutter is an irregular short dip that returns to full and never changes the pool's radius; starvation is a steady proportional dim through `served_pm` that does shrink it ("a dip dims; a sag shrinks"). input.old_string: Consequence, stated once: in the cryo bay Attention's lamp channel is absent and its other world channels
input.new_string: Consequence, stated once: in the cryo bay (and at a dock room's status glow, below) Attention's lamp channel is absent and its other world channels

input.old_string: Horror's disturbance (L3) on the EMERGENCY lamp is exempt for the same confusion, and Horror confirms it (HE-35: "never the EMERGENCY fixture subkind"): EMERGENCY stays exempt from Horror L3 disturbance. **Amendment owed
input.new_string: Horror's disturbance (L3) on the EMERGENCY lamp is exempt for the same confusion, and Horror confirms it (HE-35: "never the EMERGENCY fixture subkind"): EMERGENCY stays exempt from Horror L3 disturbance, and so is DOCK_STATUS (Horror HE-35 conformed 2026-10-28) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*. **The DOCK_STATUS exemption (user ruling X2; Attention AT-20 is the authority, CD-GDD-ALIGN) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)*.** The docked pod's dock-room status glow (LO-34) is a self-powered FIXTURE switched by SYSTEM only (Emitter EM-3, E10), `subkind` DOCK_STATUS (Emitter EM-3 owns the token). It takes no L1 gutter (it is steady; the only L1 gutter is EMERGENCY's baseline) and no L2 or L3: `M1` = `M2` = `M3` = 1000 on it (D.13), so only L0 (`output_pm`) and the warm-up and cut-fade envelopes, which are transitions outside the floor, apply. Its reason is not the gutter overlap of the cryo lamp but honesty: Attention counts it as light (`g_dock`) and never as a tell carrier (AT-20), and a system-switched glow that dipped with the web's lean or a horror's proximity would be a false tell, breaking the honest-signal contract in the room where the player reads the baseline. The exemption set of this rule and of L3 gains it; Horror HE-35 conforms (never targets it). **Amendment owed

input.old_string: Lighting maps it to a dip inside the same floor and exemption set;
input.new_string: Lighting maps it to a dip inside the same floor and exemption set (EMERGENCY and DOCK_STATUS are exempt);

input.old_string: Whether it takes the Attention gutter is Attention's call; a gutter is a presentation modulation floored at `MOD_FLOOR_PM` and never changes `lit`.
input.new_string: *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix, G6)* Exempt from the Attention tell and the Horror disturbance (AT-20, X2; LO-20): it takes no L1 gutter, L2 or L3, so its drawn energy is `LIGHT_ENERGY_PER_PM × output_pm` whenever it is on, apart from the warm-up and cut-fade envelopes.
